entities.summary:
Matthew of Aquasparta was an Italian Friar Minor and scholastic philosopher who played a pivotal role in the development of the Franciscan Order. Born in the 13th century, he was elected Minister General of the Order in 1300, a position he held until his death in 1302. During his tenure, he oversaw a significant increase in the order's membership and influence, as well as a renewed focus on poverty, simplicity, and evangelism. Matthew's writings, which were heavily influenced by the works of St. Thomas Aquinas, helped shape the order's spiritual and intellectual traditions.

Matthew of Aquasparta was a key figure in the Franciscan Order's expansion and growth, and his legacy continues to be felt in the order's mission and values. The Franciscan University in Steubenville, Ohio, is just one example of an institution that owes its founding to Matthew's influence.

Matthew of Aquasparta's writings have been translated into many languages and continue to be studied by scholars today. His works offer a unique window into the intellectual and spiritual landscape of medieval Italy, and his contributions to the Franciscan Order's development remain an important part of the order's history and identity.

In the context of medieval Italian history, Matthew of Aquasparta's role as a leading figure in the Franciscan Order was significant. The order's growth and influence during this period reflected a broader trend of religious and intellectual renewal in Italy, as well as a renewed focus on poverty and simplicity.

The Franciscan Order's expansion during Matthew's tenure was also influenced by the order's connections to the papacy and other Catholic institutions. The order's relationship with the papacy, as well as its interactions with other religious and intellectual groups, helped shape the order's development and influence.
